question: Let $f(x) = \begin{vmatrix} x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & x \end{vmatrix}$. Find all roots of $f(x)=0$. Using these, solve $f(x)=p$ for a general $p$.
explanation:
Let $f(x)=\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & x\end{vmatrix}$.
Expand the determinant using the first row.
$= x\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 \\ 1 & x\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & x\end{vmatrix} + 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & x \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$.
$= x(x^2-1) - (x-1) + (1-x)$.
Simplify the expression.
$= x^3 - x - x + 1 + 1 - x$.
$= x^3 - 3x + 2$.
Now solve $f(x)=0$.
$x^3 - 3x + 2 = 0$.
Try $x=1$. Then $1-3+2=0$, so $x=1$ is a root.
Factorize the polynomial.
$x^3 - 3x + 2 = (x-1)(x^2 + x - 2)$.
Further factorization gives $(x-1)(x-1)(x+2)$.
Thus the roots are $x=1$ (multiplicity 2) and $x=-2$.
For the equation $f(x)=p$, substitute the expression for $f(x)$.
$x^3 - 3x + 2 = p$.
Rearrange the equation.
$x^3 - 3x + (2-p) = 0$.
Thus the solutions are the roots of the cubic equation $x^3 - 3x + (2-p)=0$.

options.A: $f(x)=x^3+3x+2$; roots of $f(x)=0$ are $x=-1,-1,2$, and for $f(x)=p$, solve $x^3+3x+2=p$.
options.B: $f(x)=x^3-3x+2$; roots of $f(x)=0$ are $x=1$ with multiplicity $2$ and $x=-2$, and for $f(x)=p$, solve $x^3-3x+(2-p)=0$.
options.C: $f(x)=x^3-3x-2$; roots of $f(x)=0$ are $x=-1$ with multiplicity $2$ and $x=2$, and for $f(x)=p$, solve $x^3-3x-(2+p)=0$.
options.D: $f(x)=x^3+2$; roots of $f(x)=0$ are $x=-2$ only, and for $f(x)=p$, solve $x^3+2-p=0$.
